native/insert-text-controlled.description: Every text input is CONTROLLED_TEXT_INSERTION_COMMAND. JS lets the browser insert most typed characters into the DOM and syncs the model from the input event; the native views never edit their own text (Q40). The resulting state is the same.

native/replacement-keeps-caret.description: A replacement before a collapsed caret (autocorrection, a spelling fix, Writing Tools) leaves the caret where it was, shifted by the replacement's change in length, as NSTextView and UITextView do. JS leaves the caret after the replaced text unless the key that accepted it follows ($maybeMoveSelectionPastTrailingAcceptanceBoundary).

native/delete-content-forward.description: deleteContentForward dispatches DELETE_CHARACTER_COMMAND(false). JS dispatches DELETE_LINE_COMMAND(false) over the browser's one-character target range, which removes the same character.

native/composition-in-model.description: IME marked text is written through the model with insertText on the composing node from COMPOSITION_START_COMMAND to COMPOSITION_END_COMMAND; JS lets the browser compose in the DOM and reads the text back. No COMPOSITION_START_CHAR placeholder is inserted (desktop WebKit inserts none either).

native/select-all-menu.description: Select All from the menu or the iOS edit menu dispatches SELECT_ALL_COMMAND, as Command-A does. In a browser the menu item selects natively and only a selectionchange follows.

native/ios-hardware-tab.description: On iOS, a hardware Tab that no KEY_TAB_COMMAND handler prevents reaches UITextView, which inserts a tab character. Safari moves the focus out of the contenteditable. On macOS, insertTab: moves the focus as a browser does.

native/rtf-paste.description: A pasteboard with RTF and no HTML (copied from a native app) is converted to HTML before PASTE_COMMAND, as Safari converts it when a page reads such a pasteboard.

native/lexical-pasteboard-type.description: application/x-lexical-editor travels on the pasteboard as the type dev.lexical.editor. Safari keeps a page's custom MIME types in WebKit's private pasteboard data, so Lexical JSON copied in a browser reaches the native views as HTML and text, and the reverse.

native/drag-move-between-editors.description: A drag moved into another editor is removed from the source by the source view when its drag session ends as a move (deleteByDrag there), where JS has the drop side find the source editor's root in the shared DOM.

native/caret-format-at-run-boundary.description: A location on the boundary of two text nodes is a point at the end of the node before it, and a caret there takes that node's format, as Cocoa's typing attributes come from the preceding character. WebKit keeps its DOM caret in the node an arrow key moved through, so after moving left onto a boundary JS has the point at the start of the node after it (which $normalizeSelectionPointsForBoundaries keeps when a range starts there) and a caret with that node's format.
scenarios: TextEntry > Can insert a paragraph between two text nodes (rich)
TextFormatting > Can select multiple text parts and format them with shortcuts (rich)

native/vertical-move-by-x-position.description: ArrowUp and ArrowDown keep the caret's horizontal position in points, so where it lands depends on the fonts' metrics, which differ between WebKit and TextKit. The Linux scenario replay has no layout and keeps the character column, so the caret can land a character away from WebKit's.
scenarios: TextFormatting > Can insert range of formatted text and select part and replace with character (rich)

native/drag-selection-forward.description: A selection made by dragging, tapping, clicking or a program is forward in the model, since a native view's selected range has no direction; only a shift-arrow (a shifted key the text view handles) extends backward from the model's anchor. WebKit makes a right-to-left drag a backward selection.

native/word-move-from-range.description: With a range selected, WebKit's Option-Left and Option-Right first collapse the range to its edge and do not move further when that edge is a word boundary. The Linux scenario replay moves a word from the edge, as it models NSTextView's moveWordLeft: and moveWordRight:. Unverified: whether a real NSTextView or UITextView collapses as WebKit does is being checked on macOS; if it does, the replay changes and this entry goes.
scenarios: Navigation > native navigation > can navigate through the formatted text word by word (rich)
